chunks: I asked him about a Jewish man who committed fornication with a Muslim woman. He said: "He is to be killed."
Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Jaʿfar ibn Rizq Allāh, who said:

A Christian man who had committed fornication with a Muslim woman was brought before al-Mutawakkil. He wanted to carry out the hadd punishment against him, but the man accepted Islam. Yaḥyā ibn Aktham said: "His faith has demolished his shirk and his act." Some of them said: "He should be given three hadd punishments," and some of them said: "Such-and-such should be done to him." So al-Mutawakkil ordered that a letter be sent to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام asking him about that. When the letter arrived, he عليه السلام wrote: "He is to be beaten until he dies." Yaḥyā ibn Aktham objected, and the jurists of the garrison objected as well, and they said: "O Commander of the Faithful, he should be asked about this, for it is something that neither the Book has spoken of nor has any sunnah brought." So he wrote to him that the jurists of the Muslims had objected to this and said: "No sunnah has brought it, and no Book has spoken of it; so explain to us on what basis you made beating incumbent upon him until he dies."

So he عليه السلام wrote: "In the Name of Allah, the All-beneficent, the All-merciful. Then, when they saw Our punishment, they said: We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him. But their faith did not benefit them when they saw Our punishment—the sunnah of Allah which had already passed among His servants—and there the disbelievers lost."
He said: So al-Mutawakkil ordered concerning him, and he was beaten until he died.

key_terms.شِرْكَهُ: his prior association of partners with Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on a non-Muslim man who fornicates with a Muslim woman and then accepts Islam?
ai.summary: This report concerns the legal ruling on a non-Muslim man who committed fornication with a Muslim woman and then accepted Islam when punishment was about to be carried out. Abū al-Ḥasan al-Thālith عليه السلام supports the ruling by citing Qur'anic verses that indicate faith at the moment of divine punishment does not bring benefit. The narration presents a judicial decision grounded in Qur'anic proof.
